rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate continuing improvement on understanding proper use of programming language syntax elements from the previous courses as well as including significant expansion of the use of pointers, structures, classes, multi-file projects, recursion, exception handlings.

Write computer programs utilizing and manipulating data type including refined usage of elements from the previous course as well as c-strings, string class and object, vectors, pointers, and dynamic data allocation.
Design and document increasingly complex computer programs in an hierarchical manner and in phases (software life cycle).
Write readable computer programs utilizing professional coding standards including with respect to the new syntax, data, and design techniques addressed in this course.

rows.title: Data Structures Concepts
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate continuing improvement on understanding proper use of programming language syntax elements from the previous required courses as well as including significant expansion of the use of pointers and recursion, and adding simple inheritance.

Write readable computer programs utilizing professional coding standards for identifiers, indentations, spacing, and precondition/postcondition comments, specifically with respect to the use of data structures.
Describe efficiency-related properties of simple algorithms using "Big-O" notation: quardratic time, linear time and logarithmic time.

Design and document more complex computer programs in phases (life cycle) and an hierarchical manner, including incorporating/utilizing data structures via partial "bottom-up" design and "divide-and-conquere" approach.

rows.title: Introduction to Cloud Computing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: demonstrate knowledge and skills required to understand standard cloud methodologies
implement, maintain, and deliver cloud technologies (e.g., network, storage, and virtualization technologies)
understand aspects of IT security and use industry best practices related to cloud implementation

rows.title: Intro to Artificial Intelligence
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of Artificial Intelligence.
Demonstrate an understanding of Machine Learning with Python.
Demonstrate an understanding of Deep Learning, Neural Networks with Keras and PyTorch.

rows.title: MS SQL Database Development
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate database development techniques.
Demonstrate designing databases and administering DBMS systems.
Demonstrate writing SQL scripts.

rows.title: Advanced Visual Basic
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate Object Oriented Programming.
Demonstrate the concept of Inheritance.
Demonstrate how to design databases using SQL and connect databases to an application.

rows.title: Advanced Cloud Database Management
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Backup and Recovery Management
Integration and Automation in Cloud Database Management
Cloud Database Design and Management

rows.title: Honors Introduction to Intercultural Communication
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create solutions to address more complex intercultural communication challenges.
Identify values, norms, beliefs and practices across various cultures.
Apply advance intercultural communication theories.

rows.title: Organizational Communication
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use theoretical frameworks to develop solutions for common organizational communication challenges, such as conflict resolution, team dynamics, and crisis communication.
Demonstrate an understanding of how cultural, social, and technological factors shape organizational communication.
Critically evaluate the impact of communication on organizational culture, decision-making, and leadership effectiveness.
Apply communication theories to analyze communication patterns and structures within various types of organizations (e.g., corporate, nonprofit, public sector).
Demonstrate an understanding of key communication theories related to organizational settings, including classical, human relations, systems, and contemporary theories.
Identify and explain the major models of organizational communication, including linear, interactive, and transactional models.

rows.title: Lifelong Understanding and Self-Development
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze their personal values, skills, and interests to increase self-awareness.
Understand the different educational options available.
Understand factors that influence health and well-being.
Use effective communication skills to interact with diverse populations.

rows.title: College Success and Personal Growth
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Compose personal, academic and career goals and identify an action plan to achieve them.
Compare and contrast the validity of various perspectives on living a balanced life.
Analyze concepts, patterns and principles related to college success.

rows.title: Skills for the Helping Professions
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Practice listening and speaking from a state of equality.
Employ exercises for self-awareness and self-discovery.
Create a process for inquiry (developing interview and questioning skills).
Assemble a portfolio of facilitation techniques.

rows.title: Introduction to Public Speaking
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Conceptualizing and effectively using compelling arguments in support of a guiding thesis and organizational pattern appropriate for the audience, occasion, and across a variety of contexts.

Practicing and refining the concepts presented in the course through a variety of well prepared faculty-supervised, faculty-evaluated speeches delivered to a live audience (one to many) using effective delivery techniques.
Employing effective verbal and nonverbal practices while delivering a speech and managing communication apprehension.
Listening critically to provide constructive criticism to peers.
Plan, prepare, and deliver speeches for various forms of public oratory.
Identify and use key organizational patterns for selected methods of delivery.
Write formal outlines, conduct an audience analysis, and write a bibliography appropriate for various forms of public oratory.
Contruct logical arguments using ethos, pathos, logos, to support claims and propositions.

rows.title: Introduction to Culinary Arts and Hospitality
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify career opportunities in the hospitality industry, including food and beverage management, culinary arts, baking and pastry, lodging, restaurants, special events, managed services, attractions, tourism, and related operations.
Develop a personalized career plan outlining a chosen career pathway, including industry structure, career outlook, operational expectations, required skills, and industry trends.

rows.title: Culinary Fundamentals I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply industry guidelines for food safety and sanitation when preparing, handling, storing, and serving food.

Demonstrate safe and proper knife handling and cutting techniques by using various knives safely and efficiently, mastering essential cuts such as julienne, brunoise, chiffonade, and dicing while maintaining precision and speed.
Demonstrate proficiency using professional tools and equipment in the proper preparation of stocks, broths, soups, and sauces.
Identify and demonstrate the basic cooking techniques such as sauteing, poaching, roasting, braising, and frying.

Develop strong professional habits to demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in a professional kitchen environment. These include punctuality, organization, and effective communication. Collaborate with peers to efficiently complete tasks and maintain a positive, cooperative kitchen environment.

rows.title: Principles of Beverage Service
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe alcohol regulations.

Demonstrate the ability to recognize, categorize, and prepare different types of beverages, including wines, spirits, beers, coffees, teas, and mocktails, based on their origin, characteristics, and appropriate service methods.

Apply food and beverage pairing principles by learning to suggest appropriate alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage pairings to complement food items, enhancing the overall dining experience for customers.

Demonstrate strong professional habits to demonstrate professionalism and teamwork in a professional food service environment. These include punctuality, organization, and effective communication. Collaborate with peers to efficiently complete tasks and maintain a positive, cooperative environment.

rows.title: Hospitality Law
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate effective legal management techniques for the hospitality industry.
Evaluate legal hospitality contracts.
Plan a legal selection process for hiring employees.
Describe ADA requirements for the Hospitality Industry.

rows.title: Work Experience - Culinary
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop short term goals related to specific skills that are being developed within the work environment.
Identify on-the-job learning objectives related to their college major.

rows.title: Transmissions and Drive Train
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards when working with medium/heavy-duty manual drive-train systems.
Recognize the different medium/heavy-duty manual transmission systems.
Demonstrate clutch replacement on medium/heavy-duty manual drive-train systems.
Identify low-voltage and high-voltage components and follow safety protocols.
Use manufacturer procedures to adjust, overhaul, and replace components.

rows.title: Diesel-Electric Transport Refrigeration
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the main systems components and their functions in a transport refrigeration unit.
Perform service and troubleshooting techniques using HVACR equipment.
Define A/C high voltage electrical systems.

rows.title: Introduction to Electronic Media: TV, Radio, Film, and the Internet
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Recognize the progress of electronic media industries, and their evolution as social, political, and economic forces in U.S. society.
Develop and present original electronic media projects.
Practice ethical decision-making in the electronic media workplace.

rows.title: History of Latin American Cinema
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate comprehension of the history and formulation of motion pictures produced in Latin America.
Identify and define key film genres and the development of production techniques used in Latin America.
Identify key directors, actors, genres and specific films produced in Latin America as they relate to the historical development of the discipline.

rows.title: Introduction to Digital Media Design Principles
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify a design's reference to history, psychological impact, theories, techniques, and practices of professional design.
Evaluate and critique designs using visual vocabulary examples of two-dimensional designs from various cultures, historical periods, and aesthetic sensibilities.

Create designs that require exploration and manipulation of the basic two-dimensional elements using organizing principles of design, including balance, proportion, repetition, contrast, harmony, unity, point of emphasis, and visual movement.

Develop a portfolio of digital designs that illustrate the use of principles and elements of visual design, concept development, the creative design process, production, presentation techniques, and storytelling.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Typography
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply typographic syntax and semantics beginning with letterforms, words, lines, and columns as a cohesive whole in visual communication.
Create digital letterforms from hand rendering and inking exercises.
Apply visual hierarchy to design work, through use of letterforms, position, axis, size, scale and weight.
Utilize typographic and design terminology at a fundamental level, including type classifications and historical type references.

rows.title: Broadcasting for News & Sports
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of broadcast writing style for news and sports and the correct formatting for a variety of assignments needed for the development of a production.
Demonstrate basic understanding and working knowledge of broadcast terminology and crew positions for a production.
Perform on-camera reporting, anchoring and sportscasting.

rows.title: Digital Illustration I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate complex illustration techniques for professional quality image production.
Produce creative solutions to practical illustrative design problems using appropriate industry software.
Design visual graphics based upon written concepts.

rows.title: Game Design & Development Team
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create an interactive game.
Work in a team environment for project development and implmentation.
Utilize industry standard software facilitate animation and interactivity in a problem-focused design solution.

rows.title: Layout Design
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply visual hierarchy across a multi-page publication.
Apply meaning and tone to a multi-page publication using typographic styles.
Create a multi-page publication demonstrating a sophisticated application of grid structure.
Develop and apply a comprehensive identity/design system.

rows.title: 3D Modeling: The Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create digital 3d designs for use in video games, film, advertising and previsualization.
Create 3d characters, props and environments utilizing fundamental industry concepts and tools.
Solve real-world digital 3d design problems while working in a team environment.
Create low and high poly modeling objects and apply texture mapping to optimize models.

rows.title: Beginning News & Sports Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate beginning-level knowledge of producing stories for news and sports with emphasis on story, scheduling and crew organization
Perform beginning-level line producing for news, sports and talk shows
Act as a field producer for sports, news and interview segments

rows.title: Lighting Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding a stage light plot.
Create supporting paperwork for a lighting design.
Interpret scripts for technical lighting components through written analysis.

rows.title: Dance Laboratory IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and demonstrate technical and performance dance skills necessary for intermediate-advanced level dance projects.

rows.title: Introduction to Dance Forms
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and demonstrate short movement combinations of different dance forms.
Identify historical and cultural factors appropriate to a specific dance form.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret fundamental elements of dance composition appropriate to a specific dance form.

rows.title: Introduction to Modern Dance - II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Continue to demonstrate basic fundamental modern dance technique skills.
Evaluate and self-assess technical dance skills.
Continue to interpret and apply basic ballet and modern dance terminology and dance elements to choreographic movement phrases.
Analyze and critique dance elements of choreographic assignments, and continue to develop personal expression and interpretation of different dance phrases.

rows.title: Dance Concert Performance - IV
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate dance concert commitments, expected participation, and the practice and retaining of intermediate-advanced dance roles.
Execute intermediate-advanced level technical and performance skills necessary for duet and/or solo dance role by understanding the choreographer’s intent.
Self-assess intermediate-advanced level performance skills to illustrate artistic integrity.

rows.title: Pilates Mat II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify appropriate Pilates, level I and II vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Memorize and execute a refined skill set of Pilates, level I mat exercises, and the skill set of Pilates, level II mat exercises.
Discuss and interpret concepts of the Pilates method, appropriate for level II.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and self-assess one’s own skill set of Pilates, level I and II mat exercises.

rows.title: Introduction to Ethnic Dance Forms
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify basic dance vocabulary appropriate to a specific ethnic dance form to recognize verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate basic fundamental technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to a specific ethnic dance form.
Use critical writing skills to identify and analyze historical and cultural factors appropriate to a specific ethnic dance form.

rows.title: Introduction to Caribbean and Latin Dance Styles
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify basic Caribbean-Latin dance vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate basic fundamental technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to intro level Caribbean-Latin dance styles.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a dance concert performance.
Identify and analyze historical and cultural factors of Caribbean-Latin dance.

rows.title: Commercial Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify beginning level dance vocabulary appropriate to commercial dance to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to beginning level commercial dance.
Utilize critical writing skills to self-assess strengths and weaknesses in level I commercial dance.
Demonstrate appropriate preparations for a mock dance audition setting.

rows.title: Commercial Dance III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify level III dance vocabulary appropriate to commercial dance to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to level III commercial dance.
Utilize critical writing skills to self-assess strengths and weaknesses in level III commercial dance.
Utilize critical writing skills to present a personal resume for a dance audition.
Demonstrate preparatory skills necessary for a mock dance audition.

rows.title: Dance Repertory Workshop I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize a full-length dance within an intensive, limited time frame to be presented in a public performance.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to a specific dance genre and style within the context of a full-length dance.

rows.title: Ballet III
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet dance vocabulary appropriate to level III to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills appropriate to ballet dance level III.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level III.
Demonstrate performance skills of specific ballet compositions from famous ballets appropriate to level III.

rows.title: Dance Production I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Memorize and identify dance production terminology and theater etiquette rules.
Execute technical skills and expressive performance skills of a full length dance choreographed by faculty and/or student.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve different performance roles.

rows.title: Dance Touring Ensemble I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Execute advanced technical skills and expressive performance skills of a full-length dance to be presented as a lecture-presentation and/or performed in a pre-professional setting.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve advanced performance roles.
Use critical writing skills to identify components of performing in a pre-professional dance ensemble.

rows.title: Modern Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and modern dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a modern dance concert performance.
Identify and discuss historical factors and present-day dance concepts that influence modern dance techniques.

rows.title: Jazz Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and jazz dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level I.

rows.title: Repertory I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve beginning level performance roles assigned in guest and/or faculty repertory.
Execute beginning level technical skills and expressive performance to be performed in a formal concert setting choreographed by faculty and/or guest choreographer.

rows.title: Hip-Hop Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify hip-hop dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to hip-hop dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a hip-hop dance performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to hip-hop dance level I.

rows.title: Somatic Practices in Modern Dance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify, analyze, and describe Laban/Bartenieff concepts and terminology, and basic anatomy terminology in class discussions and written assignments.
Demonstrate Laban/Bartenieff principles and concepts to improve body-mind connectivity and move with clarity and efficiency appropriate to modern dance technique.

Use critical writing skills to identify and analyze one’s own movement patterns and apply Laban/Bartenieff principles and concepts to formulate new personal movement potentials appropriate to modern dance technique.
Observe, analyze, and assess other students' dance movement patterns.

rows.title: Choreography for the Camera
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Choreograph a diversity of dance compositions appropriate to specific location environments designed for dance filmmaking.
Analyze and criticize dance film documentations to identify various choreographic techniques and stylistic camera approaches as it pertains to dance filmmaking.
Demonstrate editing strategies in the choreographic and video production process as it pertains to dance filmmaking.
Utilize both practical and theoretical concepts of choreography and video production as it pertains to dance filmmaking.

rows.title: Special Studies in Ballet Dance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply anatomical fundamentals and practical/theoretical concepts of ballet to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to advanced ballet dance technique.
Identify advanced-level ballet dance vocabulary to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to advanced ballet dance technique.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a ballet dance concert performance.

rows.title: Tutoring Reading in Elementary Schools
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate the role, responsibilities, and limitations of a reading tutor.

rows.title: Introduction to Children with Disabilities or Delays
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Recognize children's various disabilities or delays and identify interventions based on the developmental continuum.
Evaluate the role of history and society in shaping current policies related to best practices of inclusion and serving children with disabilities or delays.
Collaborate with families and community members in supporting the inclusion of children with disabilities or delays.

rows.title: Language and Culture
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will demonstrate a broad knowledge of the global world through understanding of other languages and cultures.
Students will evaluate how language can create and neutralize biases which may be present regarding dialects, other languages, multiculturalism, and multilingualism.
Students will apply and utilize a descriptive value-neutral approach to language and culture rather than a prescriptive one.

Students will demonstrate the capacity to make informed ethical choices regarding professional application of the material of this discipline e.g., Speech Pathology, field methods, teaching, develop a commitment to accurate work, e.g., phonetic evaluation for speech pathologists.

rows.title: Survey of English Literature I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify major authors, works, themes, historical events, and literary conventions from the Middle Ages, the Early Modern period, and the Restoration.
Consider the form, content, and historical context to analyze literature from multiple genres in each period.
Produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Shakespeare's Theatre
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate an understanding of the major works, themes, and dramatic conventions of Shakespearean drama; general knowledge of Shakespeare's theatres; and general knowledge of Elizabethan and Jacobean England.
Analyze a selection of Shakespeare's plays from different critical perspectives and with regard to historical, cultural, and theatrical context.
Produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: The Image of African Americans in Literature and Films
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: identify important African-American authors, major works by and about African-Americans, and major themes in African-American literature and film;
analyze images of the African-American in literature and film and the thematic, social, and political contexts from which those images are created;
produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Survey of World Literature II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: identify major authors, works, themes, historical events, and literary conventions in a variety of world literature from 1650 to present;
consider form, content, literary conventions, historical and cultural context to analyze literature from a variety of critical perspectives;
produce college-level academic writing that demonstrates literal comprehension of texts, critical analysis, ethical use of primary and secondary sources, and correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Academic Reading and Writing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Part 2:
Read analytically to understand and respond to diverse academic texts.
Compose thesis-driven academic writing that demonstrates analysis and synthesis of sources as appropriate to the rhetorical situation.
Demonstrate strategies for planning, outlining, drafting, revising, editing, and proofreading written work.

rows.title: Critical Thinking and Writing through Literature
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Identify literary devices and use various critical theories to analyze and respond to literature from each of the four major genres: short story, poetry, drama, and the novel.
Formulate sophisticated arguments and defend them with logical, persuasive evidence.
Demonstrate proficiency in using standard written English.
Demonstrate proficiency in integrating and documenting appropriately-chosen sources, in MLA format, in an academic research essay.

rows.title: Introduction to Civil Engineering
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe the following related to engineers: their role in society, their different branches, their functions and the industries in which they work.

rows.title: Basic Mechanical Blueprint Reading
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Read and interpret views, dimensions, symbols, and annotations on mechanical blueprints

rows.title: Engineering Drawing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: apply rules of orthographic projection to create multiview drawings
create models and drawings using industry-standard CAD software

rows.title: Mechatronics II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: program and operate a micro-controller to read sensor data and control an actuator
program and operate various rapid prototyping and automation equipment

rows.title: AutoCAD II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Navigate AutoCAD interface at intermediate level
Use AutoCAD tools and functions at intermediate level

rows.title: Electric Circuits
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: solve circuits using basic laws (Kirchoff's and Ohms) and various methods and theorems

rows.title: Social Media and Digital Marketing Strategies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of the various steps that consumers and marketers go through in their decision-making process in virtual environments.
Demonstrate familiarity with social media strategies as it relates to marketing.
Demonstrate marketing knowledge in relation to digital marketing and media, and apply it to develop marketing strategies.

rows.title: Environmental Geology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Assess and evaluate the impact of natural processes such as earthquakes, volcanoes and mass wasting events on the human environment.
Assess and evaluate the impact of human activities on the natural environment through factors such as air pollution, water pollution and changing climates.

rows.title: Environmental Impacts of Industrial Development
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the major events and technological changes that influenced the industrial revolution from the 19th century to present time.
Analyze negative industrial technology effects on the environment and which technological advancements were created and/or used to remedy effects.
Identify and explain major environmental impacts as a result of industrial technology.

rows.title: Introduction to Climate Science
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Interpret climate data to explain past, present, and future climate trends.
Identify and evaluate both natural and anthropogenic factors that contribute to climate variability and change.

rows.title: Literacy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes

Define how and why business decisions are made regarding human resources and how their decision making may impact the human potential of the organization.

rows.title: Global Marketing: Selling Around the World

Conduct and analyze global marketing research.
Apply pricing and promotion strategies for global marketing.
Understand and analyze global marketing distribution methods and strategies.

rows.title: Sales, Negotiation, and Consumer Behavior

outcomes: Understand the nature of consumer behavior including how consumers make purchasing decisions, what drives them purchase, and how to evaluate purchasing results.
Understand theories of negotiation and how to handle and overcome objection in the negotiation process.
Understand different aspects of sales, how to sell, and the importance of understanding the competition.

Interpret GD&T as it applies to mechanical inspection

Summarize the necessary steps to program the PC-DMIS scanning function.

Explain the various processes used to produce metals for manufacturing.

Set up the tool and fixture.

rows.title: Honors Music Appreciation

rows.title: Rock Music History and Appreciation

outcomes: Describe and analyze rock music musical characteristics and how they relate to social movements and the specific contributions of important musicians.

Analyze the characteristics and context of music from different historical periods of rock music and distinguish between music of those different periods.

rows.title: Music Theory and Musicianship I

Perform simple rhythms, diatonic melodies, and triads by interpreting notation on the written score.

Distinguish discreet components of complex musical sounds, discern the relationship between them, and then name them.

rows.title: Applied Music (Private Instruction)

rows.title: Projects in Electronic Music

Use advanced features of a variety of recording and editing techniques in a produced mix-down of a live concert.
Write a detailed plan of a musical project that explains its function in a real world application, and the incorporation of specialized digital recording and MIDI techniques in sound design.

rows.title: Beginning Audio Production

Evaluate specific recording, live mixing and synchronization scenarios and apply effective audio production techniques.
Write a plan for a practical recording scenario and explain steps involved in its implementation.

rows.title: Class Piano III

Assess the musical effectiveness of a live piano performance by relating what they observe to more advanced aspects of piano performance methodology, in a well written concert report.

Demonstrate their ability to play notes from assigned printed music, appropriate to intermediate level piano, using correct pitches, rhythm, appropriate dynamics, fingering, and a sense of creative expression.

rows.title: Harmonization at the Keyboard

outcomes: Apply chords and harmonic patterns to accompany printed melodies appropriate to beginning level piano, using correct pitches, rhythm, appropriate dynamics, fingering, and a sense of creative expression.
Assess in a written concert report the musical effectiveness of a live piano improvised performance by relating what they observe to basic harmonization and improvisational techniques.
Define the terms and concepts associated with beginning level harmonization technique.

rows.title: Jazz Band

Produce creative and artistic expression through rehearsal and performance of jazz ensemble literature.

rows.title: Chamber Orchestra

Demonstrate, in performance, a command of musical techniques related to rhythm, pitch, tuning, articulation, balance, and expressive interpretation.

Solve musical problems in highly chromatic part writing on keyboard and on paper using principles derived from an examination of the literature.

Produce creative and artistic expression through rehearsal and performance of instrumental literature.

rows.title: Pharmacological Concepts of Nursing

rows.title: Complex Concepts

Synthesize course-related material to evaluate the historical, social, and/or cultural development of concepts and their relation to issues faced by disparate communities.

To identify and apply this knowledge of successful aging, health, and social dynamics of aging to the students’ own life and those around them

rows.title: Psychology of Human Sexuality
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the changing gender roles in today’s society and the impact to intimate relationships;
Critically examine and apply concepts and principles within human sexuality;
Demonstrate familiarity with the major issues, methods and findings within the psychology of human sexuality;

rows.title: Psychology of Adjustment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Design, conduct, and analyze a self-study relating to their own behavior in regards to psychological effectiveness in the context of Humanistic theories of personal growth.
Demonstrate the skills of active listening in communication and understand the benefits of this communication style to psychological well-being, personal growth and conflict resolution.
Explain the major humanistic theories in psychology, including positive psychology, and how they can apply to behavioral adjustment.

rows.title: Introduction to Cognitive Science
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate appropriate use of psychological terminology related to theories and concepts related to cognitive processes.
Identify the relevance of contemporary cognitive psychological research as they apply to the workplace and other everyday contexts.
Describe the theories and physiological processes of memory encoding, storage and retrieval.
Describe the neural bases of mental processes, and the brain research methods utilized in cognitive psychology.
Identify and trace the historical development of cognitive science as a discipline.
Identify how cognitive science research can be applied to everyday life.
Demonstrate an understanding of research methods in cognitive psychology and the ability to critically evaluate research in this area.
Describe theories, concepts, and research findings in the psychology of learning and cognition.

rows.title: Introduction to Communicative Disorders and Treatment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of the basic terminology related to the field of communicative disorders.
Demonstrate knowledge of the basic principles of evaluating and treating individuals with communication disorders.

rows.title: Relationships, Marriages, and Family Dynamics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will use sociological concepts to identify and distinguish the intersection of race, ethnicity, gender, social class, sexuality and other social groups on the socialization and interaction within the changing family.
Students will compare diverse patterns of family interactions, child rearing, and parenting in the US and globally.

Students will compare and evaluate positive interpersonal relationships and the key factors that contribute to their success in contrast to the major areas of family dysfunction and the effective strategies for intervention and improvement.

rows.title: Introduction to Social Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the findings of, and possible ethical issues associated with, classic experiments conducted in the field of social psychology (i.e., Stanford prison experiment, Milgram’s obedience study, Asch’s conformity study).
Analyze cognitive biases and norm violations in everyday, social situations.
Evaluate the ethical considerations of the psychological research methodology used in the field (e.g., deception, psychological harm).

rows.title: Honors Elementary Spanish I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write basic descriptive paragraphs in Spanish with clear topic sentences and supporting detail.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions in Spanish on a diverse set of cultural topics.
Use appropriate grammatical structures that include beginning-level vocabulary and verb conjugations.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics.
Demonstrate a higher level of critical thinking and professionalism in presentations.  (*Honors)

rows.title: Advanced Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of main ideas and most details of connected discourse on a variety of topics beyond the immediacy of the situation.
Build vocabulary and expand the use of more advanced grammatical structures.
Communicate effectively in spoken-Spanish using different types of discourse at the intermediate-advanced level.
Interpret and discuss a wide range of written texts (both fiction and nonfiction).

rows.title: Honors Intermediate Spanish II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write multiple compositions in Spanish at the intermediate level using description, summary, comparisons, and other modes.
Present orally in Spanish.
Incorporate idiomatic expressions and literary concepts.
Demonstrate understanding of critical analysis of literary material.
Express personal opinions and perspectives in Spanish on specific readings.
Engage in discussions about daily situations as well as cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world.
Demonstrate a higher level of critical thinking and professionalism in presentations.  * (Honors)
Produce advanced-level analytical essays demonstrating academic fluency in various literary topics.  * (Honors)

rows.title: Introduction to Statistics
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Correctly interpret a graphical display of data.
Take a statistical claim about a data set perform an appropriate procedure, and write a conclusion that addresses that claim.

rows.title: Stage Management
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a theatrical production prompt book.
Determine the duties and responsibilities of a stage manager.
Define common theatrical terminology used in stage management.

rows.title: Acting for the Camera II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Conclude a personal brand through the Actor’s Look Book.
Evaluate self-recorded performances of audition sides.
Justify character choices in an on-camera performance.

rows.title: Introduction to Drama and Acting
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate analytical skills by writing informed critiques, assessing dramatic structure, and identifying acting styles in performance.
Determine the strengths and weakness of a performance or dramatic work using proper terminology, genre identification, and style designation.
Compare and contrast performance aesthetics that make the presentation of a play a unique and dynamic art form.

rows.title: Stage Makeup
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use the concepts and techniques of stage makeup from both a technical aspect as well as an artistic aspect.
Analyze the structure of an actor’s face as well as the makeup demands for a specific character to effectively compose a makeup design.
Develop and apply original makeup designs.

rows.title: Costume Design and Construction
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze plays to assess costume requirements.
Develop themes and design concepts from a script.
Compose sketches and renderings of costume designs.

rows.title: Technical Theatre in Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate varied control and operational techniques.
Correct problems for non-responsive or non-working technical components.
Apply effective methods to meet the technical demands of back stage operations.

rows.title: Performance Ensemble
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Interpret multiple character roles through increased awareness of imagination and creative ability.
Apply various theatrical styles and apply performance techniques to each of those dramatic scenarios.
Collaborate in ensemble acting assignments.

rows.title: Work Experience - Theatre
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify three objectives of their work experience course in written form fulfilling the mandated standards of the State of California Education Code Title 5.
Develop short term goals related to the skills they are developing in the work environment.

rows.title: Intermediate Musical Theatre Techniques
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate and discuss a wide range of dramatic scripts and characterizations from diverse historical and cultural backgrounds.
Employ imagination and personal interpretation in the development of performance pieces.
Perform musical theatre pieces with accuracy, personal investment, and creative expression.

rows.title: Motion Picture Performance Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate a script for performance.
Support the behavioral life of a character for the camera in performance.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic within a professional framework of collaboration.

rows.title: Engine Repair
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use various measurement tools to check and verify engine specifications.
Assemble and disassemble a gasoline engine while following proper procedures.
Identify all major internal combustion engine components.

rows.title: Generative AI for Small Business
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Recall what is generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and how it works.
Use GenAI tools to increase productivity and create a business plan.

rows.title: Introduction to Keyboarding II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Key a minimum of 36 wpm with no more than 5 errors in a 3-minute timing.

Use the following basic Microsoft Word functions: open files, save a file, close a file, quit Word, select text, bold, undo/redo commands, get help using the Tell Me search feature, print preview, print, zoom, and spelling and grammar check.
Demonstrate proper typing posture and the ability to key using proper finger and hand placement.

rows.title: Introduction to Microsoft Publisher
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a tri-fold brochure that includes paragraphs of text, pictures, picture styles, shapes, and captions.
State three publications that can be created in MS Publisher.
Customize a flyer template by entering text, formatting text, using graphics, and resizing, moving, and aligning objects.

rows.title: MS Excel
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create, edit, save and print simple spreadsheets.
Organize, format, and sort data in an Excel worksheet.
Prepare spreadsheets for printing using the "Page Setup" options.

rows.title: Business Terminology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Define and explain the four common operation divisions in a business: production, marketing, finance, and human resource management.
Explain the four elements of operating one's own business: expenses, advertising, receipts and recordkeeping, and risk.

rows.title: Foundations of Human Resources
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify key steps in the hiring process and required paperwork.
Identify and describe performance management best practices and documentation.
Exhibit professional conduct when representing the employer.

rows.title: Career Exploration
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify personal interests, values, and strengths to determine how they align with various career pathways.
List the requirements for a specific career education program or career.

rows.title: Digital Literacy for Academic and Professional Success - Tier 1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Translate information using applications.
Create an email account.
Send an email message with an attachment.
Use a search engine to find desired information.
Demonstrate basic usage of computing devices.

rows.title: Information Technology (IT) Basics Tier 1
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the terminology and functions common to technology.
Create, manage, restore, and delete accounts.
Identify network types.
Collaborate via modern online or cloud tools.
Access digital media across multiple devices.

rows.title: Introduction to Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Identify welding equipment and their proper use.
Apply the five welding variables (arc length, amperage, travel speed, work angle, and travel angle) to achieve desired weld.

rows.title: Introduction to Digital Media Arts
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply the elements and principles of design in finished digital images and time-based work.
Create a portfolio of work demonstrating formal, conceptual, and technical development.
Produce digital images and time-based work through various digital media input and output methods using vector or raster-based software.
Examine and describe contemporary approaches, language, aesthetics and emerging media in digital art.
Evaluate and critique digital images and time-based works utilizing relevant terminology and concepts.
Safely handle and maintain digital imaging hardware and materials.

rows.title: ServSafe® Food Handler
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and interpret time temperature control when cooking, holding, cooling, and reheating.
Demonstrate knowledge to successfully pass the ServSafe Food Handler Exam.
Demonstrate proper personal hygiene to eliminate contamination and cross-contamination.
Identify food safety and how to prevent foodborne illness.
Be able to distinguish between cleaning and sanitizing.

rows.title: Introduction to Bread Making
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Explain the basics of bread making.
Define the ingredient functions of flour, water, salt, and yeast.
Explain and describe the importance of gluten.
Prepare an assortment of bread products.

rows.title: Commercial Dance I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify beginning level dance vocabulary appropriate to commercial dance to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to beginning level commercial dance.
Utilize critical writing skills to self-assess strengths and weaknesses in level I commercial dance.
Demonstrate appropriate preparations for a mock dance audition setting.

rows.title: Rehearsal and Performance in Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate and analyze a script for rehearsal and performance.
Demonstrate a strong work ethic within a professional framework of collaboration.
Create and dramatize the behavioral life of a character in rehearsal and performance.

rows.title: Ballet I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet dance vocabulary appropriate to level I to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to ballet dance level I.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a ballet dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to ballet dance level I.

rows.title: Modern Dance II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify basic Laban/Bartenieff vocabulary and modern dance vocabulary appropriate to level II to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to modern dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a modern dance concert performance.
Identify and discuss historical factors and present-day dance concepts that influence modern dance techniques.

rows.title: Repertory II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve beginning-intermediate level performance roles assigned in guest and/or faculty repertory.
Execute beginning-intermediate technical skills and expressive performance skills to be performed in a formal concert setting choreographed by faculty and/or guest choreographer.

rows.title: Overview of the Nursing Assistant Training Program
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a portfolio of all completed assignments related to the Nursing Assistant Training Program.
Identify the clinical, skills, and theoretical requirements for the Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) designation.

rows.title: Overview of the Acute Care Nursing Assistant Program
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create a portfolio of all completed assignments related to the Acute Care Nursing Assistant Program.
Identify the theoretical, skills and clinical requirements for the Acute Care Nursing Assistant Program.
Explain the difference between a Certified Nursing Assistant working in a long-term care setting vs an acute care setting.

rows.title: Personal Caregiver/Care Aide-Theory
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify and explain Personal Caregiver skills necessary to support clients with activities of daily living.
Describe infection control practices, proper body mechanics, and how to assist with mobility.
Explain different verbal and non-verbal communication strategies that ensure you are respecting client privacy, client rights, and cultural differences.
Identify and respond appropriately to common emergencies and recognize when to seek professional medical assistance.
Develop a personal self-care plan to manage stress, maintain professionalism, and prevent Personal Caregiver burnout.

rows.title: Introduction to Mental Health Services/Careers
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate knowledge of available mental health services available within the community
Demonstrate increased awareness of entry-level career paths in the mental health field
Demonstrate improved interpersonal skills relevant to working with individuals in a mental health setting

rows.title: Career Focus - Hospitality Services
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop a career plan that is designed to reflect career interests, pathways, and postsecondary options.
Describe the role technology plays in front-of-the-house and back-of-the-house jobs.
Illustrate the characteristics of customer-focused employees.

rows.title: Introduction to Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Identify welding equipment and their proper use.
Apply the five welding variables (arc length, amperage, travel speed, work angle, and travel angle) to achieve desired weld.

rows.title: Welding Metallurgy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Interpret and determine standard mechanical properties from plots of stress versus strain.
Conduct meaningful hardness, tensile, impact test and report the test results in a clear and useful manner.
Differentiate appropriate tests to be employed to determine given mechanical properties using both destructive and non-destructive techniques.

rows.title: Advanced Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Recognize the electrode and filler rod classification system for GTAW.
Differentiate between the types of polarities and their uses for GTAW.
Distinguish between types of shielding gas and their characteristics.

rows.title: Alternative Welding Processes
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate ability to operate robots and lasers safely.
Program robotic and laser arc welders.
Create laser and robotic weldments.

rows.title: Introduction to LGBTQ+ Studies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate familiarity with the major concepts, theories, methods and findings in LGBTQ+ studies.
Apply the major women, gender, and sexuality studies theories and perspectives to the issues and experiences within LGBTQ+ studies.
